kernel_changes.pipeline: QK normalization, RoPE and FP8 KV write
kernel_changes.before: Existing _qk_norm_kernel combines Q/K RMSNorm and query scale; projection, RoPE and backend KV writing have separate boundaries.
kernel_changes.after: _muse_qk_rope_cache or _qkv_epilogue writes normalized/rotated Q/K and FP8 KV; model attention bypasses its ordinary cache write.
kernel_changes.language: Triton → Triton; the projection remains a separate split-K partial producer.
kernel_changes.body_change: New cache-store epilogue folds normalization, scale, rotation and FP8 conversion; explicit BF16 round trips preserve the former sequence semantics.
kernel_changes.fusion: The QK route shares norm/RoPE/cache write in one launch. The QKV route is partial GEMM plus an epilogue launch; the whole projection is not one fused launch.
kernel_changes.applicability: TEP8, head_dim 64, local 16 Q / 2 KV heads, AITER NHD FP8 pages of size 16; decode or target verify; QKV at up to 32 rows, QK at up to 64. Actual row counts vary during the job.

kernel_changes.before: Router GEMM, fused top-k routing, pooler GEMM and pre-expert norm remain separate stages.
kernel_changes.after: route_with_shared_pooler chooses a shared epilogue or a joint packed projection followed by _joint_epilogue.
kernel_changes.language: Triton / GEMM library calls → Triton / GEMM library calls.
kernel_changes.body_change: Packed pooler/router weights and shared reduction/top-k/norm epilogues avoid separate processing of completed router/pooler results.
kernel_changes.fusion: Shared router/top-k/pre-expert norm epilogue; selected widths also share a router/pooler GEMM. Expert GEMMs remain separate.
kernel_changes.applicability: Shape guards: hidden 8192, 256 experts, top-8 sigmoid, 4096-wide pooler, contiguous BF16 input and FP32 router; at most 64 rows, with joint widths 8/16/24 in this version.

kernel_changes.before: Native-layout FlyDSL grouped experts and per-expert finalize; the MUSE_MOE_BACKEND=flydsl setting is present.
kernel_changes.after: Compact A4 target-verify experts in Triton, or AITER FlyDSL A4W4 prefill stages, followed by per-expert finalize.
kernel_changes.language: FlyDSL → shape-dependent Triton or FlyDSL; Python mxfp4_moe.py is dispatch glue.
kernel_changes.body_change: Add per-32 MXFP4 activations, compact verify work and preshuffled A4W4 weights; prefill stage 1 emits quantized intermediates/scales.
kernel_changes.fusion: Activation and quantization staging change, while the required per-expert normalization and route-weighted reduction remain explicit. Do not call the entire MoE one kernel.
kernel_changes.applicability: Compact verify requires TEP8, 32 local experts, top-8, rows divisible by 8 and no more than 512; prefill A4W4 uses at least 256 rows. Native fallbacks remain.

excluded_attributions: The SGLang monokernel interface is present in 1020, but this pair does not pass --monokernel-backend amd and has no AMD plugin execution claim.

kernel_changes.before: Ordinary SGLang attention, projection, routing, experts, residual/norm and collective launches. The monokernel interface alone does not activate the plugin.
kernel_changes.after: runtime → Muse spec → MuseMonoRunner.launch → build_layer; eligible MXFP4 layers combine attention, K2, K3 and the next eligible layer K1.
kernel_changes.language: Mixed Triton/FlyDSL/library path → FlyDSL layer kernel (the log/spec name muse_spark_hip does not identify the implementation language).
kernel_changes.body_change: Device mailbox flags connect producer/consumer stages; one launch reuses stage LDS while retaining scratch regions. The first necessary K1 and BF16-expert layers keep separate execution.
kernel_changes.fusion: Merge attention, output norm/gate and projection/reduction, routing/pooler/top-k, experts/finalize/reduction, unpooler/boundary and next-layer QKV preparation across host launch boundaries. Scratch traffic is not assumed eliminated.
kernel_changes.applicability: Both endpoint CLI logs are checked: only the new endpoint passes monokernel-backend=amd. TEP8/EP8 with 8-token DFLASH; one admitted request corresponds to 8 verify rows and two to 16. Unsupported shapes, prefill and BF16-expert layers use fallback. The exact admission is shown in this pair’s CI table.

kernel_changes.pipeline: DFlash2 draft stage-2 fusion and sharded context projection
kernel_changes.before: The draft uses the ordinary SGLang model forward; fused KV materialization is already present and is not newly attributed to 1027.
kernel_changes.after: The AMD plugin attaches DFlash2 at stage 2. Each of five draft layers has D-pre, D-attn, D-post and D-MLP launches; the context projection is TP-sharded (1024 output rows per rank) followed by all-gather.
kernel_changes.language: Ordinary Triton/library operators → FlyDSL device kernels via Python launch wrappers. The _hip spec name is not the device language.
kernel_changes.body_change: D-pre folds residual/input norm, convolution coefficients and conv0, QKV projection, per-head Q/K norm, RoPE and FP8 KV stores. D-post folds O projection, TP sum and conv1. D-MLP folds post norm/residual, convolutions, gate/up/down and TP sum. D-attn is a separate block-attention kernel.
kernel_changes.fusion: Four launches per eligible draft layer in the source call graph, not one whole-draft kernel; draft embedding/final norm, context projection/all-gather and token selection remain separate. Historical logs confirm attachment/build during setup; realized measurement launch counts remain unavailable.
kernel_changes.applicability: Only the new endpoint enables monokernel-backend=amd. Exact c1/c4/c8 server artifacts report stage 2; graph widths are [8] for c1 and [8,16] for c4/c8. Eight-token DFLASH block, TP8/EP8, matching draft architecture/cache guards. Do not extend to TEP4 endpoints without the plugin flag.

sources.role: draft routing and four launch boundaries

kernel_changes.pipeline: Ordinary verify merge with output norm/gate
kernel_changes.before: The attention partials are merged, then the existing output norm-gate kernel runs.
kernel_changes.body_change: The new body reads partials/maxima/denominators, performs split-KV reduction, rounds to BF16, and applies per-head RMSNorm and sigmoid gate before the output store.
kernel_changes.fusion: One reduce+norm+gate launch replaces separate merge and norm-gate launches; removes the completed-attention intermediate between those launches.
kernel_changes.applicability: Ordinary target-verify path, head_dim 64, output normalization enabled, and backend deferral active. On monokernel-covered MXFP4 layers the layer kernel supersedes this path; retain this candidate only for ordinary/fallback layers.

kernel_changes.before: The fused boundary yields a BF16 attention input and residual stream.
kernel_changes.after: forward_fp8 can additionally write the next projection input as FP8 plus per-row scales.
kernel_changes.body_change: The boundary kernel gains output/scaling buffers and a guarded FP8 output path; native fallback can still perform separate quantization.
kernel_changes.fusion: For its fused Triton branch, quantization is part of the norm/boundary producer, saving a separate read/quantize launch.
kernel_changes.applicability: Ordinary path when the model requests fp8_out/forward_fp8; do not transfer this benefit to the monokernel-covered layers without a trace.

excluded_attributions: The new standalone TP4 finalize/all-reduce kernel is outside this TEP8 configuration; do not list it as this pair’s executed fusion.

kernel_changes.before: The existing fused wrapper allows only page size 16 and at most 64 QK rows.
kernel_changes.after: The same QK device file is retained; wrapper guards admit pages 16/32/64/128 and a default cap of 512 rows.
kernel_changes.language: Triton → Triton; the change is in Python dispatch guards.
kernel_changes.body_change: Wrapper changes page-size and row predicates. The recorded device source hash stays identical for qk_norm_rope_cache.py.
kernel_changes.fusion: Broader applicability of existing norm/RoPE/FP8-cache fusion; no new device body is inferred from the larger cap.
kernel_changes.applicability: This pair is TEP4 with page size 16 → 128, matching the expanded page guard; target-verify row count and other shape guards still determine use. The c40 endpoint server log records rows=512.

kernel_changes.before: Already uses a one-launch TP4 HIP finalize/peer reduction on supported compact-A4 verify rows.
kernel_changes.after: Retains TP4 fusion; source is generalized to NR=4 or 8 and gains a one-shot branch used for selected TP8 widths.
kernel_changes.language: HIP/C++ → HIP/C++; Python/ctypes wrapper is unchanged in role.
kernel_changes.body_change: The device symbol becomes muse_finalize_allreduce; peer storage/arguments grow for up to 8 ranks. This TEP4 pair still compiles NR=4 and selects the two-stage protocol.
kernel_changes.fusion: Existing TP4 fusion is retained. New TP8 eligibility and its one-shot branch are not an added fusion benefit for this TEP4 pair.
kernel_changes.applicability: Both endpoints are TEP4/EP4; the wrapper’s TP4 thresholds keep the two-stage route. Actual rows must satisfy compact-A4/finalize predicates.

kernel_changes.before: The existing shared routing front admits at most 64 rows and its established FP8 joint range.
kernel_changes.after: Joint row-major routing can extend to default 128 rows, and model gating uses FP8_JOINT_MAX_M.
kernel_changes.body_change: Add wider eligibility and the row-major tile route; retain hidden/expert/weight guards and the separate shared fallback.
kernel_changes.fusion: Existing projection/epilogue fusion extends to additional shapes; not a new whole-MoE fusion.
kernel_changes.applicability: TEP4 is not rejected by _routing_front_matches: its tests are hidden/expert/weight shapes. Applicability remains conditional on packed weights and rows; client concurrency is not the kernel row count.

kernel_changes.before: Gluon muse_extend_attention serves the specialized ordinary full-attention prefill route.
kernel_changes.after: AITER backend can select muse_extend_attention_fly; Gluon remains for supported fallback/sliding paths.
kernel_changes.language: Gluon → FlyDSL for the full-attention route; Gluon remains available.
kernel_changes.body_change: New FP8 MFMA kernel uses transposed fragments, two-stage LDS loading, matrix-core row sums and explicit paged addressing.
kernel_changes.fusion: A kernel implementation/language change; no additional cross-operator fusion is established.
kernel_changes.applicability: The new endpoint enables the default FlyDSL extend route; dispatch requires gfx950 and supported FP8 Q/KV shape/layout. These TEP4 jobs retain ordinary prefill, which is outside the Muse monokernel route.

kernel_changes.pipeline: Length-balanced verify and segmented fused merge
kernel_changes.before: FlyDSL full-attention verify uses the former split scheduling; verify_reduce_norm_gate accepts four-element partial state.
kernel_changes.after: A Triton planner builds a length-balanced segment list for FlyDSL partials; five-element state selects segmented_reduce_norm_gate.
kernel_changes.body_change: Distribute KV work by sequence lengths; add segment offsets/counts and teach the reducer dispatch to accept segmented state.
kernel_changes.fusion: Planning adds a launch. The segmented output reducer retains split-KV reduction + norm/gate fusion; this is not a reduction to a single verify launch.
kernel_changes.applicability: Ordinary full-attention target verify when use_balanced_full and backend flags/shape guards select it. Heterogeneous context lengths, not just client concurrency, determine applicability.

excluded_attributions: Both endpoints are ordinary TEP4 serving: the AMD layer monokernel is not enabled by either CLI. Its captured Muse bodies are unchanged between these image digests.
TP8 finalize/all-reduce eligibility is not a new TP4 optimization.
